mcqs.question: A concave mirror has a focal length of 15 cm. An object is placed 30 cm in front of the mirror. Using the mirror formula, what is the image distance (v) from the pole?
mcqs.explanation: Using the Cartesian sign convention, f = -15 cm and u = -30 cm. The mirror formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u gives 1/(-15) = 1/v + 1/(-30). Solving, 1/v = -1/30, so v = -30 cm. The negative sign indicates a real image formed on the same side as the object.

mcqs.question: For a concave mirror, an object is placed 15 cm in front of the pole (u = -15 cm) and the image forms at 30 cm in front of the pole (v = -30 cm). What is the linear magnification of the image?
mcqs.explanation: Magnification m = -v/u (sign included). Substituting v = -30 cm and u = -15 cm, m = -(-30)/(-15) = 30/ -15 = -2. The negative sign shows the image is inverted and its size is twice that of the object.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly interprets the sign of magnification for spherical mirrors?

options.A: Positive magnification indicates an inverted image; negative magnification indicates an upright image.
options.B: Positive magnification indicates an upright image; negative magnification indicates an inverted image.
options.C: The sign of magnification does not convey any information about image orientation.
options.D: Both positive and negative magnifications always indicate upright images.

mcqs.answer: Positive magnification indicates an upright image; negative magnification indicates an inverted image.
mcqs.explanation: In the Cartesian sign convention, magnification m = -v/u. If m is positive, the image height has the same sign as the object height, meaning the image is upright. If m is negative, the image height is opposite in sign, meaning the image is inverted.

mcqs.question: A concave mirror has a focal length of 10 cm. An object is placed 15 cm in front of the mirror. Find (i) the image distance and (ii) the magnification of the image.
mcqs.explanation: Using f = -10 cm and u = -15 cm, 1/f = 1/v + 1/u gives 1/(-10) = 1/v + 1/(-15). Solving, 1/v = -1/30, so v = -30 cm. Magnification m = -v/u = -(-30)/(-15) = -2, indicating an inverted image twice the size of the object.

mcqs.question: A convex mirror has a focal length of +20 cm. An object is placed 40 cm in front of the mirror. Using the mirror formula, what is the image distance?
mcqs.explanation: For a convex mirror, f = +20 cm and u = -40 cm. The mirror formula gives 1/20 = 1/v + 1/(-40). Hence 1/v = 0.05 + 0.025 = 0.075, so v = 13.33 cm. The positive sign indicates a virtual image formed behind the mirror.

mcqs.question: For a concave mirror, an object is placed 25 cm in front of the pole and a real image is formed 50 cm from the pole on the same side as the object. According to the Cartesian sign convention, what are the signs of the object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f)?
mcqs.explanation: In the Cartesian sign convention, distances measured opposite to the direction of incident light (from object to mirror) are negative. Hence, for a real object and real image on the same side as the object, u and v are negative. For a concave mirror, the focal point lies on the same side as the object, so f is also negative. Using the mirror formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u gives f = -12.5 cm.

mcqs.question: A student forgets to assign a negative sign to the object distance and writes the mirror formula as 1/(-15) = 1/v + 1/30 for a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. What incorrect image distance will the student obtain?
mcqs.explanation: Using the student's incorrect equation: 1/(-15) = 1/v + 1/30 → -0.0667 = 1/v + 0.0333 → 1/v = -0.1 → v = -10 cm. The correct procedure (with u = -30 cm) gives v = -30 cm, so -10 cm is the erroneous result caused by ignoring the sign of u.

mcqs.question: A concave mirror has a focal length of -10 cm. If the object distance is doubled while the focal length remains the same, how does the magnitude of the image magnification change?

options.A: It becomes half of its original magnitude.

mcqs.answer: It becomes half of its original magnitude.
mcqs.explanation: For a concave mirror, magnification m = -v/u. When the object distance u is doubled (more negative), the image distance v approaches 2f (≈ -20 cm) and changes less dramatically. For example, with u = -20 cm, v = -20 cm giving |m| = 1. With u = -40 cm, v ≈ -13.33 cm giving |m| ≈ 0.33, roughly half of the previous value. Hence, increasing the object distance reduces the magnitude of magnification, approximately halving it when the distance is doubled.
